title: Vertical or horizontal bars for the tallest persons?
description: The heights of the tallest person in each class of a school are to be drawn as a bar graph. Heights are measured upward from the ground, as with the mountains in the book, so the bars are drawn vertical and the graph is a column graph.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose the direction of the bars to match the way the thing is measured. Watch for students who think only one direction is allowed, because horizontal bars would also work.

video_script.why: The child picks vertical or horizontal bars for the heights of persons, using the same reason as for the heights of mountains in the solved example.
video_script.substitution: The heights of the tallest persons in a school take the place of the heights of the mountains.
video_script.anchor: the tallest person of each class in the school of the child, ready to be drawn as bars
video_script.payoff_line: Use vertical bars, because heights are measured upward from the ground

final_answer.value: Vertical bars (heights are measured upward, easy to compare); horizontal also possible.
final_answer.spoken: use vertical bars, because heights are measured upward from the ground; horizontal bars are also possible

maths_rules: the tallest person of each class is a height, and a height is measured upward from the ground
bars that grow upward from the ground are vertical bars
a bar graph with vertical bars is also called a column graph
horizontal bars would also show the heights, but vertical bars suggest the heights better
check: the mountains in the solved example were also heights and also used vertical bars
video_script.design: The heights of persons are set beside the heights of mountains in the book. The same reason, that bars should grow the way the thing is measured, gives the direction of the bars.
